criterion: Running prose across the run board and the balance screen is set in a serif face at a measure of roughly seventy characters.
evaluation_rule: A measure is the width of a line of text. Yes if body copy, headings and table cells on the console surfaces are set in a serif family and a line of body copy runs to around seventy characters before wrapping. No if a sans-serif family carries the running prose, or if a line of body copy runs the full width of a wide window.

criterion: Every state that carries consequence on the run board, the balance screen and the certificate register is written as a word beside any colour used for the same state.
evaluation_rule: The states that carry consequence are a non-claimable batch, a lapsed calibration, an open deviation, an unreviewed override, a withdrawn certificate, a planned capacity row, a claim type on a compact figure and an unreachable contract floor. Yes if each of those reads as a word wherever it appears and green is absent from every console surface. No if any of them is signalled by a colour or an icon alone, or if a figure is tinted green so as to read as a verdict.

criterion: The balance screen prints its remaining margin as a mass in grams.
evaluation_rule: The margin is the claimable mass still available in the period. Yes if the balance screen prints a figure in grams for the margin and prints the override, restatement and finding counts as bare numerals at the same visual emphasis as the rest of the table. No if the margin reads as a status phrase such as within limits, or if a count sits inside a coloured pill.

criterion: A refused allocation on the balance screen raises an inline banner carrying the available mass beside the requested mass.
evaluation_rule: An inline banner sits in the flow of the surface that produced the act, rather than floating over it and disappearing. Yes if the banner names what was refused, prints both masses, says what would change the outcome, and every figure already on the screen stays as it was. No if the refusal appears as a floating toast, or if the banner carries only a generic failure message.

criterion: An empty console collection says so in a sentence, and a surface awaiting data says the surface is loading.
evaluation_rule: Yes if an empty batch register, an empty certificate register and an empty restatement list each render a sentence naming what is absent, and a surface still fetching prints a loading line. No if an empty collection renders as a blank frame or as a bare table head, or if a loading surface renders as an empty one.

criterion: An unsatisfied issuing condition on the certificate wizard names the record that would resolve the block and links to that record.
evaluation_rule: The eight issuing conditions are shown as eight statements on every step of the wizard. Yes if an unsatisfied statement names the blocking record, such as an unreviewed override on a lot, and offers a link to it, and every control on the screen leaves the block standing. No if the statement reads as a generic failure, or if any control on the screen sets the condition aside.

criterion: The withdrawal screen prints the recipients by name and the statements that become void before the person confirms.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the screen lists each recipient who will be notified as a named row and lists each downstream statement the recipient must stop making, both before the confirming control. No if the screen prints a count of recipients instead of the list, or if the lists appear only after confirmation.

criterion: Signing a certificate is a separate act on the review step that states the recipient will file the document with a regulator.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the review step renders the document, carries one control whose label names signing rather than saving, and prints a sentence saying the recipient files the document with a regulator. No if signing shares a control with moving between steps, or if the consequence sentence is absent from the review step.

criterion: The console carries one persistent top bar whose controls match the role the reader holds.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the same top bar appears on every console surface and an auditor session shows reading and export controls alone. No if navigation moves into a side rail on some surfaces, or if a mutating control renders for a reader whose role forbids the act.

criterion: Labels take the grotesk, identifiers and column figures take the monospace, and hierarchy comes from size with one heavier stroke on the two largest steps.
evaluation_rule: Yes if field labels, table headers and the top bar are set in a sans face, lot references and masses in tables are set in a fixed-width face whose figures align down a column, and only the two largest heading steps carry a heavier stroke. No if masses in a column fail to line up, or if three or more stroke levels appear across the console.

criterion: The public routes show photographed pellets and waste imagery that reads as mixed contaminated material.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the pellet imagery reads as a photograph of real granulate rather than a render, and the waste imagery shows mixed, coloured, contaminated textile rather than clean sorted offcuts. No if the pellets read as a synthetic render, or if the waste imagery shows tidy single-colour material.

criterion: Motion across the product reads as eased, with entrances and exits settling once and each transition declared against a named property.
evaluation_rule: An eased transition accelerates and decelerates on a curve rather than overshooting its endpoint. Yes if panels, banners and menus settle in one movement and each transition names the property it animates. No if any element overshoots and springs back, or if a transition is declared across every property at once.

criterion: Headings on the public routes come into focus from a blur as the reader reaches them, resolving through one shared distance and duration.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a heading below the fold begins blurred and transparent, sharpens as the reader arrives, is legible before the movement ends, and every heading on every public route uses the same distance and duration. No if headings only fade in, or if a figure counts up as it changes.

criterion: Text across the product meets WCAG AA contrast at every size, sits at twelve pixels or above, and every icon-only control carries a label.
evaluation_rule: Yes if body copy, labels and disabled text all clear the AA ratio against their ground, the smallest rendered text measures twelve pixels or more, focus rings are visible on every focusable element, and each icon-only control carries a text label or an accessible name. No if any text falls below twelve pixels, or if an icon-only control reaches a reader as an unnamed glyph.

criterion: The focus treatment differs from the hover treatment, and keyboard navigation reaches every control a pointer reaches.
evaluation_rule: Yes if tabbing to a control produces a visibly different treatment from hovering the same control, and every menu, dialog and wizard step is reachable and operable from the keyboard alone. No if focus and hover render alike, or if any control is reachable only under a pointer.

criterion: The genealogy graph, the balance screen and the certificate wizard each reflow into a single column at a phone width.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the graph becomes the nested list, the balance table becomes one figure per row, and the wizard becomes one condition per row, each carrying the same facts as the wide arrangement. No if any of the three shrinks its wide arrangement into an unreadable version of itself.

criterion: Every route holds its layout from a narrow phone to a wide desktop under one breakpoint system.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each public and console route renders usably at a phone, a tablet and a desktop width, the breakpoints repeat the same widths across the whole product, the document itself stays free of sideways scrolling, and a wide table scrolls inside its own container. No if a route forces the document to scroll sideways, or if two different sets of breakpoint widths appear.

criterion: The reconciliation view leads on the mass balance residual, and the replay result gives agreement the same visual emphasis as disagreement.
evaluation_rule: The residual is the mass the period cannot account for, and a reader expects the figure to be other than zero. Yes if the residual is the first and largest figure on the reconciliation view, and the replay result renders a matching figure and a differing figure in the same size, colour and weighting. No if the residual is buried among the other five figures, or if a disagreement is styled as an alarm and an agreement as a reassurance.

criterion: The palette across the public routes reads warm rather than neutral, with the quiet text a clear step lighter than the reading text.
evaluation_rule: The brief names six roles by the job each does and states no colour value, so the build picks all six. Yes if the page ground is a warm off-white rather than a grey or a pure white, and a secondary label reads as quieter than body copy at a glance while still being legible. No if the ground is neutral grey or pure white, or if a secondary label is either indistinguishable from body copy or too faint to read.

criterion: The package manifest shall strictly adhere to the checklist obligation set: the client framework, the API framework, the database driver and the mail client must be the entire dependency tree. A static manifest walk AND a runtime import-graph traverse must both resolve clean before a PASS is recorded.
evaluation_rule: A runtime dependency is a package named in the dependencies block of the app package manifest, not a transitive lock entry and not a development-only tool such as Vite, a bundler or a test runner. Yes if every runtime dependency is the Preact client framework, the Hono API framework, the PostgreSQL driver, the SMTP mail client, or a direct requirement of one of those four, and no module under the source tree imports a package outside that set. No if the manifest names a second database driver, a cache or queue client, a scheduler package, an object-store client, a mail vendor SDK, an outbound HTTP client aimed at the weighbridge, the control system, the laboratory or customer reporting, or any package no obligation in the brief reaches. The statement's runtime import-graph half is discharged by the static scan just described: the whole source tree is present, so an import scan that returns nothing outside the permitted set settles the graph, and an uninstalled node_modules is not a reason to leave this unresolved.

criterion: The schema must enumerate exactly the entities the data model enumerates and nothing more. A static schema diff AND a runtime information_schema count must both prove zero tables, columns or seeded rows beyond the enumerated set.
evaluation_rule: The enumerated set is the thirty-six entities the Data model section names, from site through legal_hold. Yes if the schema creates one table for each enumerated entity and no table beyond them, and the seed writes only the rows the Data model section pins -- the three sites, the three balance periods, the four batches, the two energy instruments, the seven carbon breakdown lines and the other tabulated rows. No if the schema creates a table for a concept the entity list does not name, such as a sequence counter, an annotation, a notification, an idempotency store, an account or a certification period, if a table carries a column for a quantity no entity description states, or if the seed writes a row for an entity the brief never tabulates. The statement's runtime information_schema count is discharged by counting the CREATE TABLE statements in the schema and the tables the seed inserts into; that count is what information_schema would report.

criterion: No scheduler, message queue, cache or background worker shall exist for work the obligations did not ask for. A static process and timer scan AND a runtime handle audit must both show nothing for the criterion to pass.
evaluation_rule: A scheduler is any timer that fires work on a clock -- a cron expression, a repeating interval, a delayed callback that schedules recurring work, or a job library. Yes if the source registers no such timer, imports no message queue or broker client, holds no cache layer keeping derived figures between requests, and starts no background worker process beside the API. No if a module registers a cron or interval job, imports a queue or broker client, keeps a module-level map of computed figures that survives a request, or the container image or process manager starts a second worker process alongside the API. A run close recorded as queued and the persisted carbon figure with its cache_valid flag are records the brief requires, not infrastructure, and neither counts against this criterion. The statement's runtime handle audit is discharged by the timer, import and entrypoint scan just described: nothing can hold a handle at runtime that no module in the tree opens.

criterion: The source must contain no outbound client for the weighbridge, the control system, the laboratory or the customer reporting system. A static import scan AND a runtime outbound-connection observation must both witness no client targeting any of the four.
evaluation_rule: The four sources are the weighbridge, the control system, the laboratory and customer reporting; each pushes records in through POST /api/inbound/{source} and the app opens no connection back to any of them. Yes if no module constructs an outbound HTTP, socket, FTP or vendor-SDK client addressed at one of the four, and those four names appear only in the inbound route, the reconciliation integration_ages report, the schema, the seed and the client surfaces that display them. No if a module calls fetch, a HTTP client library, a raw socket or a vendor SDK against a weighbridge, control system, laboratory or customer reporting endpoint, if configuration or environment reading carries a base URL, host or credential for any of the four, or if a polling routine reaches out to collect what the source is meant to push. The statement's runtime outbound-connection observation is discharged by the static scan: a connection no module opens cannot be witnessed at runtime, so an empty scan settles it.

criterion: No in-memory substitute for a table, no fixture file standing in for a seeded row and no log sink standing in for the mail service may survive anywhere in the tree. A static type map AND a runtime row-provenance check must both confirm that every entity is read from the declared store.
evaluation_rule: The declared store is postgres reached at DATABASE_URL, and mail leaves through mailpit over SMTP at SMTP_HOST and SMTP_PORT. Yes if every entity the API returns is read from a Postgres query, every seeded row named in the Data model section is inserted into a Postgres table, and every mail act named in the Mail table is handed to an SMTP client. No if a module holds an array, object map or JSON fixture file standing in for a table, if a route answers an entity from that structure rather than from a query, if seeded rows are declared as JavaScript objects served directly instead of being inserted, or if sending a mail is recorded by writing to a log, a console or a file instead of over SMTP. The statement's runtime row-provenance check is discharged by tracing each route's answer back through the source to the query or the in-process structure that produced it.

criterion: The ledger invariant must be expressed exactly once and every write path must reach that single assertion rather than restating the check. A static single-definition audit AND a runtime fault-injection pass over every write route must both record the refusal coming from the one shared code path.
evaluation_rule: The ledger invariant is that attached claim never exceeds available claim, so credits_available_g never falls below zero and an over-allocation is refused with available_g and requested_g. Yes if that comparison is written in exactly one place and every path that moves credit -- an allocation, an inter-site transfer, a period close and a restatement -- reaches its refusal through that one site. No if a route module restates the comparison in its own words, if the allocation handler and the arithmetic module each carry their own copy, or if the same rule appears inverted in a second module so that two sites could drift apart on the same figure. The statement's runtime fault-injection pass is discharged by following every credit-moving write path in the source to the site that raises its refusal and seeing whether the paths converge on one site.

criterion: Every derived integer shall strictly floor through the one shared helper; no module may round a figure another module floors and no call site may bypass the helper. A static call-graph walk AND runtime arithmetic spot-checks must both flag any bypass.
evaluation_rule: Every derived integer in this product is floored, never rounded and never carried at half. Yes if a single shared helper performs that floor and every derived figure -- dry mass, credit granted at a consumption, recycled content_bp, a conversion factor, a byproduct share, a carried-forward figure and a running weighted content -- is produced through it. No if any module calls a rounding function, relies on a division that leaves a fraction to reach a stored integer, or writes its own floor expression at a call site, so that two modules could disagree on the same figure. The statement's runtime arithmetic spot-checks are discharged by reading each derivation in the source and naming which floor, rounding or bare division it reaches.

criterion: One idea must carry one identifier across the whole source; a consumption must never be a consumption in one module and a usage in another. A static symbol-pair scan AND a runtime declaration-versus-use trace must both find no drift.
evaluation_rule: One idea carries one identifier across the client, the API, the arithmetic and the schema; the brief's word for a row of consumed mass is a consumption, not a usage. Yes if each domain noun the brief names -- consumption, output, lot, batch, deviation, override, credit movement, restatement, resolution, record entry, approval period, inbound record -- appears under that one name in table names, column names, function and variable names, and payload fields. No if a single concept is a consumption in one module and a usage or a draw in another, if a credit movement is a ledger entry in one layer and a movement in the next, or if a payload field renames the column it carries so a reader must map two words onto one idea. The statement's runtime declaration-versus-use trace is discharged by the static symbol scan across the schema, the arithmetic, the API and the client.

criterion: Unit suffixes must be carried consistently in identifiers in every layer, not the API surface alone: a mass must end in _g, a proportion in _bp and a carbon figure in _mg_per_kg. An identifier audit AND a runtime payload scan must both satisfy the rule.
evaluation_rule: The suffix rule is that a mass ends in _g, a proportion, content, moisture, factor or uncertainty ends in _bp, a carbon figure ends in _mg_per_kg, energy ends in _kwh and capacity ends in _kg. Yes if identifiers carry the suffix at every layer -- schema columns, arithmetic variables and helper parameters, API payload fields, and client component props, state and local variables. No if a client or arithmetic identifier drops the suffix while the API field keeps it, if a quantity is carried in an identifier named mass, amount, total or value with no suffix, or if a suffix is attached to a figure of a different quantity, such as a _g on a proportion. The statement's runtime payload scan is discharged by reading the object literals the routes return and the props and state the client components declare.

criterion: The arithmetic that derives every claim must live in its own module and the operational-record layer must never import it. The import graph AND a runtime module-load trace must both confirm the one-way dependency direction the brief states.
evaluation_rule: The arithmetic layer is the code that derives every claim and figure and has no writable input other than the operational record and the versioned methods; the operational-record layer is the routes and storage that people at a plant write to. Yes if that arithmetic lives in its own module or directory and the import direction runs one way, the arithmetic reading the operational record while no operational-record module imports the arithmetic. No if a write handler for an intake, a run, a deviation or an override imports the arithmetic module to compute a figure inline, if the arithmetic module and a record-writing module import each other so the dependency runs both ways, or if the derivation is spread across route files with no module of its own. The statement's runtime module-load trace is discharged by the static import graph, which fixes the load direction between the two layers.

criterion: The pinned seed values must be read from one seed definition wherever they are needed and must never be duplicated as literals, including threshold constants, across modules. A literal-duplication scan must show zero restatements before a PASS is recorded.
evaluation_rule: A pinned seed value is a literal the Data model section fixes -- a site reference with its nameplate_kg and contracted_kg, a balance period id with its carry_over_limit_bp of 2000, a batch mass, the conversion factor of 8000 basis points, the carbon breakdown lines summing to 4260000, and the primary-data threshold of 5000 basis points. Yes if each such value is written once in one seed or constants definition and every other module reaches it by reference. No if a threshold such as 2000 or 5000 basis points is retyped inside an arithmetic or route module, if a seeded reference such as BP-DEMO-N6-2026H1 or LOT-N6-0001 appears as a literal outside the seed definition, or if two modules each declare their own constant for the same pinned figure.

criterion: A rule or literal set that governs more than one route must be defined once and referenced by every site, never restated. A static symbol lookup AND a runtime reference count must both resolve to exactly one defining site.
evaluation_rule: A governing set is a validation, an enumeration or a literal list that more than one route depends on -- the categories post_consumer and pre_consumer, the confidence values, the four inbound source names, the resolution outcomes reissued, withdrawn and unaffected, the balance period states open and closed, and the role names. Yes if each such set is declared once and every site that needs it imports it from that one definition. No if two route modules each declare their own array or inline literal for the same set, if a client surface restates a set the API already defines rather than reading it from a shared module, or if the same validation is written twice in different words so the two could diverge. The statement's runtime reference count is discharged by counting the import sites that reach the one definition, or the inline restatements where no single definition exists.

criterion: No exported symbol may be unreferenced, and no symbol may be exported solely because it is used inside its own module. A tree scan AND a runtime coverage walk must both find every export consumed outside its defining module.
evaluation_rule: An export is a symbol another module can import; a symbol used only inside its own file does not need to be exported. Yes if every exported symbol in the source tree is imported by at least one other module, counting the application entry points and the test files as consumers. No if a module exports a helper, constant, component or type that no other file imports, if an export outlives the removal of its last call site, or if a symbol is exported only so that it can be reached from elsewhere in its own module. The statement's runtime coverage walk is discharged by resolving every import in the tree, tests and entry points included, against every export.

criterion: One mechanism for one idea must carry one persisted name; no concept may be implemented twice under different names. A static schema-catalog audit must find no two mechanisms for the same duty.
evaluation_rule: A mechanism is a persisted structure that carries out one duty -- a table, a view, an enumerated column or a status field. Yes if each duty in the data model is carried by exactly one such mechanism under one name, so a lot's disposition, a certificate's state and a balance period's state each live in one named place. No if the schema carries two tables for the same duty under different names, if a state is recorded both as a column on the row and again as a separate history or status table that the same code path writes, or if the same concept is spelled one way in the schema and another way in the API it feeds.

criterion: No module may grow past the point where its responsibilities can be read as one unit. The largest modules must be restructured or the criterion stays failed; a static size audit AND a runtime load-trace review must both confirm the unit stays within its readable bound.
evaluation_rule: A module is a JavaScript or TypeScript source file; a schema or seed SQL file is data rather than a module and is out of scope here. A module stays within a readable bound when one reader can hold its responsibilities as a single unit, which in a tree of this shape means it does one layer's work for one part of the domain. Yes if no source module runs past roughly eight hundred lines and each of the largest modules holds one coherent responsibility. No if a route, arithmetic or data-access module runs to several thousand lines, if one file carries every route in the API, or if one module mixes storage, arithmetic and HTTP handling in the same file. The statement's runtime load-trace review is discharged by the static size and responsibility audit of the same modules.

criterion: Values crossing the database boundary must be converted exactly once at the data-access boundary. Re-coercion with Number() at call sites must be absent; a static coercion scan AND a runtime type-trail check must both show the conversion happens at one point.
evaluation_rule: Values crossing the database boundary are the integers Postgres returns for bigint, numeric and count columns, which the driver hands back as strings. Yes if that conversion to a number happens exactly once, inside the data-access layer that runs the query or in one configured driver type parser, so every consumer downstream receives a typed integer. No if a route, an arithmetic module or a client call site wraps a value in Number(), parseInt or a unary plus after it has left the data-access layer, or if the same column is converted in one module and left as a string in another so two callers see different types. The statement's runtime type-trail check is discharged by following each column from the query that reads it to every site that consumes it.

criterion: The submit control on every form shares its trailing edge with the fields it submits.
evaluation_rule: A form's fields are its text inputs, selects and text areas, and its submit control is the button that sends them. The leading edge is the left edge of those boxes and the trailing edge is the right edge. Yes if, on the sign-in form and the enquiry form, the submit control and the fields above it share both edges at a phone, a tablet and a desktop width, so the block reads as one column. No if the fields stretch to the full width of the form while the submit control is sized only to its own label, so the trailing edge is ragged, or if the two edges agree at one width and part at another.

criterion: The sign-in surface is reshaped by the declared breakpoint system rather than holding one fixed card at every width.
evaluation_rule: The breakpoint system is the one set of widths the product declares for a narrow phone, a tablet and a wide desktop. Yes if the sign-in surface changes its layout across those widths, taking a different card width or a different internal arrangement at a tablet than at a wide desktop, so a query in the declared system governs it. No if the card holds the same pixel width and the same pixel height from a wide desktop down to a tablet and changes only once the viewport itself becomes narrower than the card, which is the card clamping to the window rather than a breakpoint reshaping the surface.

criterion: The sign-in surface fills the tablet viewport rather than leaving most of it empty.
evaluation_rule: The fold is the area visible without scrolling, 768 by 1024 at a tablet width. Yes if the sign-in card occupies at least half the height of that fold at a tablet width, so the surface reads as a designed page rather than a small card adrift in empty space. No if the card takes less than half the fold's height, or if the card holds the same height at a tablet as at a wide desktop so that the empty space around it simply grows with the window.

criterion: A heading sits on the same margin as the body copy it introduces.
evaluation_rule: The margin is the left edge of the text column on a left-aligned surface. Yes if, on every public route, a heading and the paragraphs beneath it begin at the same left edge at a tablet and at a desktop width, so one unbroken vertical line runs down the text column. No if a heading is indented from its body copy or the body copy is indented from its heading, if the two agree on one public route and differ on another, or if the offset appears at one of the two widths and not the other.
